headline: Trump signs EO waiving Graham Act Russia sanctions/tariffs two days before Oct 18 deadline
dek: Trump invoked Sec.115 national-interest waiver to suspend the Graham Act's core tariff/sanctions provisions: 500% duty on Russian goods, 100% duties on top-5 importers of Russian crude/gas (India ~1.8M bpd, China ~1.2-1.5M bpd, Turkey etc.) and top-5 sanctions-evasion facilitators, plus most…
sources: White House executive order 'Implementing the Lindsey O. Graham Sanctioning Russia and Iran Act of 2026' (Oct 16); relayed by CNN (Oct 19), Bloomberg (Alicia Diaz), AP
fault_line: Betrayal of Ukraine and Congress (bipartisan outrage, 'Russian asset' framing, 110K-like HCR post) vs pocketbook pragmatism — were the tariffs ever going to work, or would they just tax US diesel before the midterms?

sections.what_happened: Trump invoked Sec.115 national-interest waiver to suspend the Graham Act's core tariff/sanctions provisions: 500% duty on Russian goods, 100% duties on top-5 importers of Russian crude/gas (India ~1.8M bpd, China ~1.2-1.5M bpd, Turkey etc.) and top-5 sanctions-evasion facilitators, plus most foreign-person sanctions (Secs 102(a),102(d),102(e),103-111,117). Waivers have NO end date; earlier EO sanctions preserved. Law had been signed Sept 18; deadline was Oct 18.
sections.what_verified: CNN Oct 19 ('Tariff Man' piece, Ed Mills/Raymond James: 'eviscerates any real enforcement'); Bloomberg: waiver tied to diesel-price push before Nov 3 midterms; AP: White House did not explain national-interest basis; Deccan Herald: Jaishankar raised refinery concerns with Rubio at UNGA; readus247: Sec.4(d) no end date, justification report unpublished; Telegraph India: India's imports expected steady at ~1.8-1.9M bpd October
sections.what_disputed: White House certified waiver 'in the national interests' (Sec.115 authority is in the statute); duties were formally imposed then suspended — Trump can reimpose. Existing Russia sanctions architecture untouched. Supporters frame it as avoiding fuel-price spike pre-midterms, not capitulation.
sections.why_matters: The empire's economic cannon jams on its own fuel prices: Washington builds the heaviest sanctions weapon in years (500% duties) then refuses to fire it because diesel is at record highs. India and China keep their Russian crude; the sanctions arc bends to the pocketbook. Verifiable numbers only: 500%, 100%, 1.8M bpd.
sections.context: Background: Trump signs EO waiving Graham Act Russia sanctions/tariffs two days before Oct 18 deadline (MISSED earlier — ELEVATION: major sanctions change)
